# scenario G2: Trip A offline
# argv: --trip-fixture trip_a_mry_nyc.json --offline --balance UR=160000 --card Chase Sapphire Preferred --transfer-date 2026-09-15
# exit: 0

TRIP A - Monterey to New York, Jan 15-18 2027
Round trip, economy. Real cash prices captured by Tsuki on 2026-09-07 for January 2027.
Source: Google Flights + Marriott.com, captured 2026-09-07 by Tsuki. Transcribed verbatim.

Wallet (supplied at runtime - nothing is assumed)
  UR: 160,000   valued at 1.00 cents/point
  cards: Chase Sapphire Preferred

Transfer date: 2026-09-15 (ratios and bonuses are looked up on THIS date, not on the travel date - the ratio that applies is the one in force when you transfer)

==============================================================================
FX rates used (table as of 2026-09-08):
  1 EUR = 1.1620 USD [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]   sourced 2026-09-07 (4 days old)   [BOOKING-SITE IMPLIED: back-derived from the Novotel Madrid dual-currency quote ($747.81 / EUR643.57 = 
1.1620). One booking page on one date - NOT a market rate.]
  1 GBP = 1.3540 USD [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]   sourced 2026-09-08 (3 days old)   [SOURCED on 2026-09-08. Replaces the 1.2700 placeholder, which had no source and understated the London 
hotel by about $42. A sourced rate still goes stale - confirm before trusting.]
  1 CAD = 0.7256 USD [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]   sourced 2026-09-08 (3 days old)   [SOURCED on 2026-09-08. Added so the captured CAD 44.60 tax on the real SFO-MAD Aeroplan award can be 
scored instead of carried as an unknown. Confirm before trusting.]
  !! FX RATES REQUIRE CONFIRMATION. EUR is back-derived from a single hotel quote; GBP and CAD were looked up on a date and go stale. Every foreign-currency total below inherits that 
uncertainty.
  !! Supply a rate with --fx GBP=1.36 to take responsibility for it and clear the marker.
==============================================================================

Valuation: cash is scored at 1.00 cents per point ($1.00 cash = 100 points-equivalent). Points and cash are ranked on this single yardstick.

Data problems flagged, NOT silently fixed
  - Trip A and Trip B both start Jan 15 2027. They appear to be ALTERNATIVES, not one itinerary. Scored separately; totals are NOT combined.
  - Flights are priced for 1 adult. The hotel is priced for 2 guests. This inconsistency is reported, not silently corrected - nothing is doubled.

Per-leg detail

A1 - MRY-JFK round trip, Jan 15-18 2027, economy, 1 adult
  Verdict: CASH - Cash is cheaper: $367.00 vs at least $430.00 on points at 1.0cpp. The carrier-imposed surcharge is UNKNOWN, but it can only ADD to the points side, so cash wins whatever it
turns out to be. Do NOT burn points here.
  Cash: $367 American (SkyWest/American Eagle) MRY-JFK, 1 stop PHX 2h59, 6:00am-7:00pm, 10h
  Points: JetBlue SFO-JFK nonstop (badge 21.3k pts one-way, x2 for round trip)
        UR 43,000 -> JetBlue TrueBlue 43,000 @ 1:1 [Chase Sapphire Preferred]
        spend: 43,000 UR
        stranded: 400 (within the unavoidable transfer increment)
        metal: B6 (source: captured), cabin Y
  Surcharge: UNKNOWN - this is NOT $0.
        Break-even: points beat cash only if the surcharge is below $0.00.
        Cannot model a surcharge for 'JetBlue SFO-JFK nonstop (badge 21.3k pts one-way, x2 for round trip)'. No surcharge rule for JetBlue TrueBlue on B6 metal, NA-NA Y departing US. This is
NOT zero - the figure is simply not known.
  note: Google Flights headline: 'Cheapest from $367'.
  note: Listed cash prices are ROUND TRIP. The points badges are labelled '(one-way)'.
  note: American AAdvantage (the two $367 options) is NOT a Chase UR transfer partner.
  note: Alaska Mileage Plan (the $389 option) is NOT a Chase UR transfer partner.
  note: Only the JetBlue option maps to a UR partner (TrueBlue), and it is also the most expensive cash fare.
  FLAG: INFERENCE: round-trip points cost is modelled as 2x the one-way badge. Google showed only a one-way badge; the return leg's award price was not captured and may differ.
  FLAG: Two options depart SFO, not MRY. Positioning Monterey->SFO is not priced anywhere in this data.
  FLAG: Region classified on SFO-JFK, the route actually priced. The leg is named MRY-JFK but the priced option departs SFO.
  UNVERIFIED: Points price for JetBlue SFO-JFK nonstop (badge 21.3k pts one-way, x2 for round trip) is UNVERIFIED (google_badge_unverified). Google Flights '21.3k pts (one-way)' badge, 
doubled for round trip. Google badges often reflect dynamic revenue pricing, NOT partner saver award space. Not confirmed against Seats.aero. Metal is unambiguous (JetBlue nonstop, JetBlue's
own aeroplane), but no surcharge row exists for JetBlue TrueBlue, so the surcharge resolves to UNKNOWN rather than to $0.
  UNVERIFIED: Program attribution for JetBlue SFO-JFK nonstop (badge 21.3k pts one-way, x2 for round trip) -> JetBlue TrueBlue is an ASSUMPTION; the source did not name the program.
  UNVERIFIED: JetBlue SFO-JFK nonstop (badge 21.3k pts one-way, x2 for round trip): the carrier-imposed surcharge is UNKNOWN, so this points option CANNOT be scored against cash. It is NOT 
$0. Points beat cash only if the surcharge is below $0.00.

A2 - Marriott NYC, Jan 15-18 2027, 3 nights, 1 room 2 guests, Traditional King city view, 'Long Term Stay rate'
  Verdict: CASH (POINTS UNPRICED) - Marriott Bonvoy IS a UR partner, but no award price was captured, so the points option cannot be scored. Points would win below 83,326 points.
  Cash: Traditional King city view, Long Term Stay rate, 3 nights ($597.00 room + $236.26 est. taxes/fees)
        ! Plus a daily destination fee charged at check-in, amount not captured, not payable with points.
  note: Room 3 nights $597.00 + estimated taxes/fees $236.26 = $833.26 total.
  note: A daily destination fee is charged at check-in and CANNOT be paid with points. It is owed on a points stay too.
  note: Marriott Bonvoy IS a Chase UR transfer partner at 1:1.
  FLAG: NO Marriott Bonvoy award price was captured. The points option therefore cannot be scored - only a break-even is reported.
  FLAG: The daily destination fee amount was not captured, so no total including it can be computed.
  FLAG: The destination fee is NOT modelled as a MandatoryFee because its AMOUNT was never captured. Inventing a figure to make the model look complete is exactly what this tool must not do.
It remains a note.
  UNVERIFIED: No award price was captured for Marriott Bonvoy. Break-even is 83,326 points: below that, points beat cash; above it, pay cash. NOT scored - input missing.
